messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Broken build: namespace issues.
parts:
One instance of our issue is in src/prob/distributions/multivariate/continuous/inv_wishart.hpp. There is a using statement for stan::math::determinant, defined in src/stan/math/matrix.hpp. The problem is that the stan::agrad::var version of determinant() exists in stan::agrad, defined in src/stan/agrad/matrix.hpp.

The simple solution is not what we want: adding a using statement for stan::agrad::determinant. That will create a dependency from our probability library to the stan::agrad::var objects.

Should we move the src/stan/agrad/matrix.hpp functions into namespace stan::math?



Daniel

PS. I am not sure how this worked before.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Broken build: namespace issues.
parts:
We shouldn't be calling determinant(S) or determinant(W) there anyway, as the underlying Eigen function does not take advantage of the presumed positive definiteness of these matrices. Better to call .llt() and get the determinant and inverse from L.

Ben

On Tuesday, April 17, 2012 12:47:05 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
One instance of our issue is in src/prob/distributions/multivariate/continuous/inv_wishart.hpp. There is a using statement for stan::math::determinant, defined in src/stan/math/matrix.hpp. The problem is that the stan::agrad::var version of determinant() exists in stan::agrad, defined in src/stan/agrad/matrix.hpp.

The simple solution is not what we want: adding a using statement for stan::agrad::determinant. That will create a dependency from our probability library to the stan::agrad::var objects.

Should we move the src/stan/agrad/matrix.hpp functions into namespace stan::math?



Daniel

PS. I am not sure how this worked before.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Broken build: namespace issues.
parts:
On 4/17/12 6:37 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> We shouldn't be calling determinant(S) or determinant(W) there anyway,
> as the underlying Eigen function does not take advantage of the presumed
> positive definiteness of these matrices. Better to call .llt() and get
> the determinant and inverse from L.

Sounds sensible.

Any volunteers to follow Ben's advice? I'd do it, but
my linear algebra's still too shaky to be trusted
in this setting (unless someone writes all the formulas
out more directly for me -- I'm happy to be the code monkey).

> On Tuesday, April 17, 2012 12:47:05 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
>
> One instance of our issue is in
> src/prob/distributions/multivariate/continuous/inv_wishart.hpp.
> There is a using statement for stan::math::determinant, defined in
> src/stan/math/matrix.hpp. The problem is that the stan::agrad::var
> version of determinant() exists in stan::agrad, defined in
> src/stan/agrad/matrix.hpp.
>
> The simple solution is not what we want: adding a using statement
> for stan::agrad::determinant. That will create a dependency from our
> probability library to the stan::agrad::var objects.

Right -- we don't want dependencies from stan::prob to stan::agrad.

The using statement could be added at a higher level if
we stuck to header-only usage, but we're not doing that, either.

So what we need is a template specialization declared in
the instantation file in src/stan/agrad/.

Then, if we import all the headers, argument-dependent lookup
should find the version from the right namespace.

> Should we move the src/stan/agrad/matrix.hpp functions into
> namespace stan::math?

That's also OK, but we can't in general have this because
of the std:: functions we implement auto-dif for.

> Daniel
>
> PS. I am not sure how this worked before.

All of the header definitions (not just declarations)
were in place for the single translation unit. At that
point, it's just argument dependent lookup again.

- Bob

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Broken build: namespace issues.
parts:
For the record, I'm pretty certain this is a linker issue and not a namespace issue.  Specifically, it's not finding stan::math::determinant in libstan.a for some reason.  My library foo is weak, however the symbol list

[mbrubake@rincewind bin]$ nm -gC libstan.a | grep determinant
0000000000005590 T stan::math::determinant(Eigen::Matrix<double, -1, -1, 0, -1, -1>)
0000000000000000 W stan::agrad::var stan::agrad::determinant<stan::agrad::var>(Eigen::Matrix<stan::agrad::var, -1, -1, 0, -1, -1> const&)
0000000000000000 W stan::agrad::var stan::agrad::determinant<double>(Eigen::Matrix<double, -1, -1, 0, -1, -1> const&)
0000000000000000 W Eigen::PartialPivLU<Eigen::Matrix<stan::agrad::var, -1, -1, 0, -1, -1> >::determinant() const

suggests that when the .o files are combined together, something different is happening with the stan::math version than the stan::agrad version.  (See the T vs W prefix.)  This is causing the linker to not find the math versions.  I had a theory that this had something to do with the fact that both object files had the same name but playing in that direction didn't yield any results.

About using LLT here, Bob check out multi_normal_log_chol for an idea.  The determinant of a matrix A = L*L^T is the product of the square of the diagonals.  I.E., det(A) = \prod_i L(i,i)^2 or, more stably, log(det(A)) = 2 * \sum_i log(L(i,i)).

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] low-triangular * vector product?
parts:
It should work (in theory) much like the triangular solvers work (see mdivide_left_tri).  You take a triangular view of the matrix and then perform your operation based on that.  Eigen has specializations for triangular matrix products so it should call those when needed.  However, that's unlikely to work properly right now if you have mixed types.  For the time being you may be stuck with evaluating out the full thing untoi lwe have better handling of mixed types and are more tightly integrated with Eigen's operations.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] low-triangular * vector product?
parts:
The easiest thing to do is call Stan's multiply().
It will probably be faster than promoting double to var
and calling Eigen's specialized triangular multiply
because of the auto-dif savings.

Better yet would be to write a version of multiply()
for triangular matrices into in agrad/matrix.hpp.
It would have tighter loop bounds and use different
dot_product lengths based on which row you're using
from the matrix. To avoid promotion, this requires
four implementations ({double,var}*{double,var}).

Longer term, of course, we want to have our
expression template cake and eat it, too.

- Bob

On Wednesday, April 18, 2012 3:38:26 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Ben -- are you not on the build list to get the
build errors e-mailed from the Jenkins?
I guess not but I can read them from Google Groups.

The problem is here (with an identical problem for Wishart):

   TEST(ProbDistributionsInvWishart,DefaultPolicy) {
     Matrix<double,Dynamic,Dynamic> Sigma;
     Matrix<double,Dynamic,Dynamic> Y;
     double nu;

     Sigma.resize(1,1);
     Y.resize(1,1);
     nu = 1;
     EXPECT_NO_THROW(inv_wishart_log(Y, nu, Sigma));

The new implementation is balking on 1x1 covariance matrices.

I think the code should work for 1x1. I think it is balking on the fact that Sigma and Y are not allocated or maybe are allocated with zeros (or maybe are allocated with ones on Linux because it worked for me). So, the fix that I just pushed (which I did in the other NOTHROW case) was to

Sigma.setIdentity()
Y.setIdentity()

which got Jenkins back to normal.

For now, I added a test to throw a domain error (or
whatever the policy is) if either Wishart or inverse Wishart
get a 1x1 covariance matrix and changed the unit tests
to match and everything's passing agin.

But I see no reason why it can't work for 1 x 1 matrices,
and it's not being checked, so it must be one of the
linear algebra ops throwing an exception.

We can certainly fix it more if need be, but I am inclined to say that stan should throw a domain error in the 1x1 case. I could see why the underlying Eigen functions should support 1x1, but I would guess that the majority of the time when this occurs in stan, it is a mistake on the user's part.

Ben
